newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan financials rise on outlook for futures.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan financials rise on outlook for futures.

text.p: Taiwan financial shares were outperforming a cautious market at mid-morning on Thursday on news that Singapore and Chicago would list Taiwan stock-index futures in January, brokers said.
The indexes to be used by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Singapore's SIMEX are both weighted heavily toward Taiwan financial and big-capital shares.

Cathay Life, the third most active issue, gained T$5 or 2.82 percent to T$182 after 85 minutes of trade, while the weighted Taiwan index was up only 0.71 percent to 6,992.98 points. The financial sector as a whole rose 1.63 percent.
Shares in the "big three" state-run banks -- Chang Hwa, Hua Nan and First -- each rose T$3 to T$157, T$131 and T$168 respectively.
Taiwan is developing a futures exchange that will offer stock-index futures and options amonth other contracts, but it will not open before July 1 at the earliest.

The CME and SIMEX contracts aim to tap Taiwan's liberalising financial market, although Taiwan regulators have not said if they would authorise local trading of the overseas-listed Taiwan stock index derivatives.
Brokers cautioned that the rising financial sector created pressure for investors to take profits.

"Because many banks are expected to have better profits next year, financials should remain the market leader for some time although some profit-taking may also emerge at their highs," said Joe Chiou of Taiwan Securities.
